stepsIntro: Eight steps from an applicant submission to a separate simulated permit issuance.

system.note: Every component is built. Signed-in personas and the public act through the browser, the service governs authority, and the model only proposes.

permit.note: The primary journey SYN-APP-001. Decisions, money and issuance stay with deterministic services and named personas.

authority.note: Sources own their facts. The registry owns identity, and a write becomes authoritative only after the source adapter accepts a version.

agents.note: The Agent Operator wakes and runs each agent. The agents recommend, the reviewer decides, and six simulated departments only read the property master.

muse.note: The model reaches the application only through the adapter. It has no edge to the database and no edge to a source. The applicant help answer and the council briefing use the same exchange, and Muse Image makes the permit-type icons.

verify.note: Evidence comes from the services and the checks. No figure counts as complete until the stored record exists. The operations screens carry the audit log and the in-process checks.

legend: Dashed outline, built locally, not deployed
status.note: The status record holds 57 outlined requirements, 57 implemented, 57 verified, 22 tasks, and 22 verified tasks.

steps.d: The applicant submits immutable plans and documents for a fictional tenant improvement.
The service stores the submission, hashes the payload and opens the intake work.
The application builds a bounded context from versioned fictional documents and source snapshots.
A live Standard call returns a structured proposal, and the application validates it.
A Data Steward records the match or the correction against exact evidence.
A Permit Reviewer makes an actual review decision on the recorded evaluation.
The approved catalog prices the case, and Finance confirms the allocation.
A separate issuance action records the permit, and a retry returns the same artifact.

p_applicant.b: Selectable in the dropdown. It manages its own authorized profile, its drafts, its submissions and its requested responses.
f: Cannot see other applicants, match candidates or staff evidence.
A persona label grants no authority on its own.

p_steward.b: Carries explicit Intake Clerk, Domain Steward and Domain MDM Steward grants for scoped queues.
f: Reviews quality issues, proposes source corrections and decides permitted identity links.
Cannot approve or issue permits, and cannot allocate money.

p_reviewer.b: Carries explicit Permit Reviewer and Issuing Officer grants.
f: Review approval and the separate Issue permit action stay different server-enforced actions.
Cannot edit credentials, source facts or receipts.

p_admin.b: Carries separately declared Administrator, Governance Lead, Data Owner, Finance and Auditor grants.
f: Configuration rights do not create business approval rights.
Finance allocation and owner approvals follow their own grants and state rules.
Sets the agent processing policy in Administration, Agent processing. Does not wake or run the agents.

browser.b: Jinja screens with small vanilla JavaScript enhancements, served by the local service on loopback. They include Administration, the applicant portal at /apply, the property master, the town map, the City of Acme website and the operations screens.
f: The browser holds no model credential and no write path to a source.
Current master, submitted, proposed and issued values stay visually distinct.

api.b: One Python 3.12 service. It owns the action checks, the state machine, the deterministic arithmetic and the model adapter.
f: Binds loopback only.
Every authoritative action is checked here against its grant and its expected version.

musead.b: Builds the bounded request, calls the model and validates every returned identifier, excerpt and citation.
f: Strict JSON Schema, allowlisted identifiers, bounded inputs and outputs, no web search, no tool calls, concurrency one.
A rejected proposal is recorded as rejected and creates nothing.

gov.b: Domains, datasets, contracts, assignments, queues, grants and the field correction routes that connect them.
f: Explicit grants per action, checked in the service.
Configuration rights never become business approval rights.

ingest.b: Immutable snapshots, raw payload hashes, validation, quarantine, source ordering, freshness and denominators.
f: Three persisted in-process adapters stand in for the Permitting, GIS and ERP and Finance sources.
Approved does not mean synchronized.

registry.b: Stable canonical identities, proposals, crosswalk decisions, provenance, trusted views and reversible links.
f: Owns identity, not source-owned facts.
A link correction commits a new crosswalk version and claims nothing about the source.

permits.b: Profiles, immutable submissions, documents, evaluations, recommendations, actual decisions, issuance and impact review.
f: One approved versioned catalog drives the fee assessment.
The model never makes a reviewer decision.

finance.b: Exact assessments, payment events, allocations, reconciliation, exceptions and the separate issuance action.
f: The variable component is rounded once, with a half up rule.
An outstanding balance blocks issuance.

db.b: One SQLite database, one durable outbox for publication and acknowledgements, and an append-only action trail.
f: The trail records accepted and denied sensitive actions.
It is append-only storage, and the page makes no tamper-proof claim.

evidence.b: Requirement mappings, acceptance, supplementary and scenario outcomes, manifests, artifact hashes and browser checks.
f: No figure counts as complete until the stored record exists.
The register currently holds no passed or recorded outcome.

muse.b: The model endpoint used for the live extraction in the primary chain.
f: Standard mode only, and never a contributor model.
The live primary-chain run succeeded. Replay never counts as live evidence.
The provider balance and the no-cash path are unverified.

The same endpoint also writes the applicant help answers, the council briefing and the what-if proposals. Replay is the default for all of them. They share the live call cap 2, the daily allowance 10 and the error stop.

src_permit.b: Owns applicant profiles, applications, contractor registration, decisions and issuance.
f: A correction becomes authoritative only after this adapter accepts a version.
The adapter acknowledges the accepted version to the application.

src_gis.b: Owns parcels, official addresses and units, and zoning facts. Since phase 2 it is a simulated service inside the application, with 69 parcels, 71 addresses and no outside calls.
f: Snapshots feed the registry and its trusted views.
The registry records lineage, and it never edits the parcel.

src_erp.b: Owns business licensing, finance accounts and payment events.
f: The outbox publishes a payment command here, and the adapter acknowledges it.
Money is never set by a model output.

status.b: The one architecture status record behind this page. It holds the counts that the status panel and this node report.
f: 57 requirements outlined, 57 implemented, 57 verified.
22 tasks, 22 verified. Complete: redesigned interface, local user test.
20 acceptance tests with 20 passed, 8 supplementary checks with 8 passed, and 11 scenarios with 11 recorded.
Live Muse primary chain succeeded.

agents.b: Two agents that the Agent Operator wakes and runs. The intake agent has seven nodes and the adjudication agent has five. Every run is recorded with a per-node trace.
f: Intake: classifier; field extractor and document quality check in parallel; address locator and completeness check in parallel; duplicate finder; router.
Adjudication: rule loader; rule evaluator; condition builder and precedent check in parallel; disposition.
Only the Agent Operator holds agent.toggle, agent.run.intake and agent.run.adjudication. The City Administrator sets the processing policy in Administration, Agent processing.
Optional automatic processing uses a durable work queue and one worker that is off by default and not enabled on Render. It uses built-in deterministic logic and never calls the model provider.
Confirm records the reviewer's decision, and a held recommendation cannot be confirmed. Revert needs a reason.

admin.b: City Administrator only. Tabs are Permit types, Appearance and Users and roles. The rest are Agent processing, Reason codes and the Configuration log. Appearance holds the permit-type icons, which Muse Image can generate. Users and roles shows which staff roles may run agents.
f: The catalogue has 17 permit types.
A configuration change applies only to new intake.
Agent processing sets the policy: manual, or automatic as work arrives. It decides nothing about a case.

propmaster.b: The shared parcel record at /property/{parcel} and a server-rendered SVG town map at /map. The map loads no outside tiles and makes no network calls.
f: The address locator proposes a parcel link and never approves it.
A permit decision is blocked until the parcel link is approved and confirmed.
Parcels are textured with 17 bundled local WebP image tiles, made with Krea 2 at build time. The City view uses them too.

subs.b: Tax and assessor, fire and life safety, code enforcement, utilities, sanitation and police read property master fields.
f: Each department reads fields and writes nothing back.
Access is set in config/property_subscribers.json.

p_public.b: Anyone who opens the City of Acme website without signing in. They reach the public pages and the Permits in my community lookup.
f: Sees only the allowlisted public fields of a permit: no names, notes, documents, contact details, fees or findings.
A total under 3 shows as fewer than 3. A case that is not public gets the same answer as a case that does not exist.

ops.b: City Administrator only. It holds the operations dashboard, the audit log, the support desk and the in-process checks, at /ops/dashboard, /ops/audit, /ops/support and /ops/checks. Each has its own grant.
f: The support desk answers an applicant's Ask the City request and records the reply as an answer from the City.
The eight checks report historical seed cases as not applicable or as exceptions, never as passes.
Every figure on the dashboard carries its definition, and synthetic history is excluded unless included on request.

help.b: Answers an applicant's questions about the permit process, the rules for their project and their own application, from a cited source bundle the server builds. Offered on /apply, on the application form and on the tracker.
f: Muse Spark writes the answer when live use is on, and a labelled replay fixture answers by default. A validator refuses any answer that is uncited, misquotes a source or promises an outcome.
If the answer is refused or nothing matches, the applicant sees the matching ACME rule text. Ask the City sends the question to the support desk.
The audit record carries identifiers and the outcome, never the text of the question.

city.b: The fictional public site under /city/: home, permits and applications, services and Permits in my community at /city/community. Applicants reach their own pages through it.
f: The community lookup reads a dedicated public model with 17 allowlisted fields, rate limited and read only.
A banner says the persona switcher is for the demonstration only.

policy.b: City Administrator only. A person defines a what-if change, such as raising the side and rear fence limit from 6 ft to 7 ft. The service then scores a synthetic year of cases under the old and new rules.
f: Runs are immutable and every edit is a revision. Muse Spark can explain a run or propose a change, and a person decides.

Save as a draft rule change makes an ordinary draft. Approval follows the approval policy: by default one administrator may approve, and the independent setting requires a different administrator (config/approval_policy.json).
Only rule limit, operator and fee changes convert to drafts. The rest stay simulation only.

briefing.b: A briefing on a what-if run for the council. It is built from typed facts of the stored run, and Muse Spark can write it through the policy_brief task.
f: Every figure must match a cited fact or a rule source, or the whole response is refused.
No staff-time, throughput, savings or revenue claim is allowed, and the synthetic population is called synthetic.
Replay fixtures are labelled demonstration fixtures, not live recordings.

insight.b: City Administrator only, at /insight/city. A district-shaded town map with exception dots, filters for type, outcome, period and category, a monthly trend and a definition beside every figure.
f: Start a what-if from this view opens the policy agent with the current type and category.
The insight map and the public community lookup read the same permit history through separate models.

synth.b: One deterministic generator, generate_synthetic_year in portal_intake/scenarios.py, builds a dated year of fictional permit cases from versioned distributions. It runs no agent and writes no audit event.
f: Records are flagged synthetic and the default reset loads none of them. The demo-synthetic mode loads them.
The what-if policy agent adapts the same generator for its population, so no second generator exists.

museimg.b: The image model that drew most of the permit-type icons: 14 of the 17 came from 14 calls to muse-image-1.0 on 2026-10-28. A City Administrator can generate more in Administration, Appearance tab.
f: Icons are decorative and carry no record data.
Applicants cannot generate icons.

p_operator.b: Holds the agent_operator grants. It wakes, sleeps and runs the intake and adjudication agents, processes a bounded selection of waiting cases and reads the run history.
f: Home is Agents, with Intake agent, Adjudication agent and Agent runs.
Cannot decide, issue or configure. The reviewer decides.
Only this persona holds agent.toggle, agent.run.intake and agent.run.adjudication.

facts.y: Parent owned. It changes only when a recorded source changes.

status.y: The status panel and the status node are rewritten from it at each accepted phase transition.
